question.leadin: Name these French kings named Louis.
question.text: This Louis, whose wife was Marie Antoinette, was guillotined during the French Revolution.
question.clue: Crippling debt and a lack of credit forced this man to call the Estates-General in 1789.

swap.leadin: This government was headed by Philippe Petain.
swap.text: Name this Nazi-approved government that ruled France from a namesake city during World War II, while the Germans occupied Paris.
swap.answerHtml: Vichy France [or the French State; or État français; prompt on France]
swap.clue: It held the Vel'd'hiv raids, which sent people to the Drancy camp, and ran under the motto of "Work, Family, Fatherland".

question.leadin: This person was granted an audience with the king after predicting the outcome of the Battle of Rouvray.
question.text: Name this woman, nicknamed the Maid of Orleans, burned at the stake in 1431 for heresy after fighting for the French against the English at battles such as Patay and the siege of Jargeau.
question.clue: Guillaume de Flavy stranded this figure outside the gates of Compeigne by lifting a drawbridge too soon, allowing John of Luxembourg to capture this leader, who was then subjected to a trial led by Bishop Pierre Cauchon.

swap.leadin: This man survived a 1962 assassination attempt by the OAS, a group of French dissidents who wanted to stop the negotiation of the Evian Accords.
swap.text: Name this French President, the founder of the Fifth Republic, who had earlier led the Free French forces during World War II.
swap.answer: Charles Andre Joseph Marie de Gaulle
swap.clue: This man was criticized for a speech given at Montreal's Expo 67, and he signed the Evian Accords.

question.text: Pope Zachary's deposition of Childeric III marked the end of this dynasty in France, whose most notable ruler was Clovis I.
question.clue: In a confiict caused by a princess's refusal to follow her husband's religious practices, this dynasty defeated Amalric, king of the Visigoths.

swap.leadin: It was besieged by forces under the Earl of Salisbury, who cut off its access to the Loire.
swap.text: Name this city, where the French won their first significant victory after their loss at Agincourt by repelling a 6-month siege.
swap.clue: This city gave its name to a movement for constitutional monarchy begun by Philippe Egalite, who opposed the Legitimists.

question.leadin: The name of these events comes from the slings supporters used to break windows.
question.text: Give this term referring to two rebellions against the government of France in the 1600s.
question.clue: Noble members of the parlements began this event by refusing to pay higher taxes during the Franco-Spanish War.

swap.leadin: The tide of this battle is alleged to have turned when the losing side ran from the battlefield in order to protect their camp and all the loot inside.
swap.text: Name this battle in which Frankish infantry defeated forces under Abd ar-Rahman. It took place after an appeal by Odo the Great as an invading force approached the River Loire.
swap.answerHtml: Battle of Tours (or the Battle of Poitiers; or the Battle of the Palace of the Martyrs)
swap.clue: The Duke of Aquitaine, Odo the Great, fought for the winning side of this battle, during which Abd al-Rahman died.

question.leadin: Medieval historians argue over whether there was a "Renaissance" associated with this man.
question.text: Name this Frankish ruler whose court included Alcuin of York and the biographer Einhard.
question.answerHtml: Charlemagne [or Karl the Great; or Charles the Great; or Carolus Magnus]
question.clue: His rearguard was defeated by the Basques at the Battle of Roncevaux Pass, and he split his territory amongst his three grandsons in the Treaty of Verdun.

swap.text: Foch famously counterattacked at this 1914 battle outside of Paris. French victory during it stopped the German's Schlieffen Plan offensive and set the stage for prolonged trench warfare.
swap.answerHtml: First Battle of the Marne [or Premiere Bataille de la Marne, prompt on partial answer]
swap.clue: The key moment in this battle came when reserves arrived in taxi cabs from Paris, prompting a surge which caused Helmuth von Moltke's forces to retreat and abandon the Schlieffen Plan.

question.text: As Lieutenant-General of the Police, de la Reynie investigated this scandal that exposed many French aristocrats for hiring fortune tellers for illicit purposes. The king's mistress Madame de Montespan was implicated in this scandal.
question.clue: This affair began when the Marquise [mar-KEEZ] de Brinvilliers [brin-vil-YA] was executed in 1676 for the murder of her father and brothers. During this affair, Madame de Montespan, the mistress of Louis XIV, was suspected of participating in black masses.

swap.text: Named after the third son of King Philip III, members of this French royal family included Charles VII and Louis XI, and they were replaced by the Bourbons.
swap.clue: In order to liberate one king of this family from their captors, their son was forced to sign the Treaty of Bretigny, and this dynasty came to power when Philip the Fortunate was chosen as king over Joan of Navarre and Edward III of England.

question.leadin: The French Third Republic was best by a series of political scandals in the late nineteenth century.
question.text: Though this man successfully wrangled Egyptian concessions and planned the building of the Suez Canal, his involvement in Panama was a debacle which ended with his conviction for defrauding investors and bribing politicians.

swap.leadin: It came to an end in 1940, and its leading statesmen included Raymond Poincare, Edouard Daladier, and Aristide Briand.
swap.text: Identify this period of French history bounded by the Franco-Prussian and the Second World Wars.
swap.clue: Paul Painleve served as Prime Minister during this government and, in order to acquire indemnities, Raymond Poincare ordered its invasion of the Ruhr.

question.leadin: Dena Goodman argued that Jean-Jacques Rousseau caused a decline in attendance at these events in the 1780s by ranting against "the disorder" of women's ideas, thus prompting widespread female participation in the French Revolution.
question.text: Name these French Enlightenment era gatherings hosted by women like Madame du Deffand, in which people exchanged political and philosophical ideas.
question.clue: During one of these events, a woman embroidered and broke up fights amongst Girondins.

swap.leadin: In 1980, Jean-Yves Blot (jahn-eev bloh) led an expedition that recovered a bronze swivel-gun from the site of this event.
swap.text: Identify this event, an account of which was written by Alexandre Correard (KOH-ray-ar) and Henri Savigny (ahn-ree sav-yen). Hugues Duroy de Chaumareys (yoog doo-wah doo SHOO-mah-ray) was court-martialed following this event.
swap.answerHtml: the shipwreck of the Méduse [or the raft of the Méduse; or descriptions of the wreckage of the Méduse; accept Medusa in place of Méduse; prompt on shipwreck; prompt on cannibalism]

question.text: Talleyrand collaborated on secret talks with tsar Alexander I and the abduction of the prince d'Enghien with this duplicitous police minister, who was expelled from France by Napoleon in 1812.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about a French monarch and his reign.
swap.text: This son of Blanche of Castile repelled revolts by Raymond VII of Toulouse and eventually signed a treaty of Paris with Henry III of England.
swap.clue: This king of France who led the Seventh and Eighth Crusades.

question.leadin: Name some people or things relating to the Genoese Republic.
question.text: This Corsican nationalist fought so successfully against the Genoese that they finally called in the French to crush him, which they did, but then in 1768 forced Genoa to give Corsica to them.
question.clue: This Corsican general served as president of the Corsican Republic before it was captured by France. He later fought with the British to free Corsica from French occupation.

swap.text: Much of Darnton's work deals with France, which was the home of this school of historiography. Developed by Marc Bloch and Lucien Febvre, this group focused on long-term social history.
swap.clue: A 60 year history of this group was authored by Peter Burke.
